landmarks.name: Merlis Belsher Place
facts: It is the campus hockey arena, which hosted the 2024 national women's university hockey championship.
It officially opened in 2018.

landmarks.name: St. Andrew's College
facts: It is a theological college of the United Church of Canada.
It was the Presbyterian Theological College until 1925, when it was renamed after the United Church of Canada formed.

landmarks.name: Engineering
facts: Its original building was designed by Brown & Vallance and first opened in 1912.
Its college awarded its first degrees on April 26, 1916, to just three civil students.

landmarks.name: Canadian Light Source Synchrotron
facts: It is a particle accelerator facility, one of Canada's largest investments in science.

landmarks.name: College of Education
facts: Its college was founded in 1928, and in 1964 it took over the teacher's colleges in Saskatoon and Regina.

landmarks.name: Arts
facts: Its seven-storey tower and its theatre opened in 1961, two years after its classroom wing.

landmarks.name: Agriculture Building
facts: It is a large glass building built between 1988 and 1991, with a seventh floor added in 2000.

landmarks.name: Murray Building
facts: It was the main library's first home when it opened in 1959; a seven-storey addition was finished in 1974.
It is named after the university's first president, like a park in Saskatoon.

landmarks.name: Physics
facts: Construction began on May 10, 1962, when Nobel laureate Sir John Cockcroft turned the first sod.

landmarks.name: Diefenbaker Canada Centre
facts: It holds the papers and legacy of a prime minister from Prince Albert, Saskatchewan.
It is a museum and archive named after the prime minister who led the country from 1957 to 1963.

landmarks.name: Saskatchewan Hall
facts: It was designed by Brown & Vallance, like the Administration Building.
Completed in 1912, it was the university's first student residence.

landmarks.name: Administration
facts: It houses the president's office.
It was designed by Brown & Vallance and built from 1910 to 1912.

landmarks.name: Peter MacKinnon Building
facts: A campus museum moved into it in 2005, after the building was renovated.

landmarks.name: Kirk Hall
facts: It is home to the School of Environment and Sustainability, founded in 2007.

landmarks.name: Law
facts: Its college is the oldest school of its kind in Western Canada, training future attorneys and judges since 1912.
Its college was established in 1912 and hired its first professor, a classics teacher, in 1913.

landmarks.name: Gordon Oakes Red Bear Student Centre
Wollaston Hall
facts: It is a family apartment tower in McEown Park.
It was added to the McEown Park complex in 1976.

landmarks.name: Souris Hall
facts: It is a nine-storey apartment complex for students with families, named after a prairie river.

landmarks.name: Assiniboine Hall
facts: It is an eleven-storey apartment house for students, named after a prairie river.

landmarks.name: Seager Wheeler Hall
facts: It is a fourteen-storey residence named after a Saskatchewan pioneer of wheat breeding.

landmarks.name: St. Chad Chapel
facts: Since 2007 it has housed the graduate students' association's headquarters, called GSA Commons.
